setting: The story is set among the chaebol families of a parallel-world, present-day Seoul. Everyday life revolves around business wars, shareholdings, arranged marriages, and the alliances and rivalries between chaebol houses. Romance set against the families' business wars, and the public talk that puts any photographed affair at the top of the business pages, are where the whole story's tension lives.

statNotes.selfId: Rises when she chooses something her family would not have chosen for her, in front of someone who will report it. Falls when she performs the daughter the name requires.
statNotes.secrecy: Falls when the relationship becomes legible to anyone outside the circle - a driver, a house staff member, a photographer outside a hotel, a line in a business column. Rises when a plausible reason is on the record first.
statNotes.mood: Driven by the family's calendar, what the companies are doing to each other this quarter, and how the last exchange with the target member ended.

composed: These {n} women are one chaebol family, and {org} is the family's company. {name} exists only in this story.

The family name is {family}. A member who carries that surname is a daughter of the house; a member with any other surname is a cousin, the child of one of the house's daughters, and belongs to the family just as fully.

They grew up inside it together - the same schools, the same weddings, the same board dinners - and each of them holds a seat in the family and in the company that the others can see. Rival houses exist around them and do business with and against them constantly, but no member of this cast belongs to another house. Whatever groups these members belong to outside this story are not part of this world and must never be mentioned.

ONLY the members listed in MEMBER PROFILES are named people in this story. Everyone else is unnamed - a driver, a house staff member, an executive, a reporter - and no other name may be used, not even in passing or over a phone.

identities.name: Rival heiress
identities.background: [Identity: Rival Heiress] You are the daughter of another chaebol house, and your family competes directly with {name}'s in the same industry. Advantage: You are her equal - one of the few people in this circle who does not have to look up at her. Disadvantage: Every interaction between you is taken as business first, including the sincere ones. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

events.text: You are seated next to each other at the same banquet and the whole room is watching what you say
Both families bid on the same project and you are looking at her from across the table
A reporter asks for your view of her family and you give an answer with nothing in it
Afterwards she is waiting in the car park, and what she asks about is not business

identities.name: Fallen heiress
identities.background: [Identity: Fallen Heiress] Your family was once part of this chaebol circle too, and lost everything a few years ago. You still have to face the circle's social life, but your standing is not what it was. Advantage: You understand this circle's rules better than anyone, because you were once inside it too. Disadvantage: Everyone knows where you stand now, you included - so anything she gives you looks like charity. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

events.text: Someone at a banquet remembers your name, with sympathy in their voice
You are wearing something two seasons old and she says nothing, only stands a little closer to you
Somebody brings up what happened to your family in front of you and she changes the subject

On a formal engagement you have brought flat shoes so she can change out of her heels when she is tired
She slips her schedule and goes out alone, and you know where to find her - and you do not report it

Advantage: You do not belong to the chaebol circle, so you can ask what nobody else dares to. Disadvantage: Your relationship began in a deception - whatever it becomes later, that stays a knot buried inside you. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

events.text: You slip into a chaebol banquet and she sees immediately that you do not belong there

identities.name: Main Member's Ex-Girlfriend
identities.background:
[Special Identity: Main Member's Ex-Girlfriend]
- You and {name} were lovers, breaking up years ago due to {reason}
- You still keep {keepsake} to this day
- Now the two families' business has brought you back together: awkwardness, complicated feelings, things left unsaid. Early interactions involve deliberate distance, averted eyes, polite but distant
- People in the circle may or may not know about your past. As the game progresses, you may reconcile or go your separate ways

reason: being young and not knowing better
keepsake: the plane tickets from your trip together as a couple

modes.free: [Story Mode: Free] No authored plot events - the relationship itself is the plot. Affection grows slowly. Focus on details and subtle tension: what is said in front of staff, what is said in the car, what is never said at the table. No rushing into relationship.
modes.romance: [Story Mode: Romance] Ambiguous & Romantic. Natural progression with mutual attraction. Members flirt once their own stage in [Affections] allows it (section 9), never before.
modes.pressure: [Story Mode: Pressure] Press attention and family obligation higher, secrecy changes doubled. Being seen together carries weight: a photographer outside a hotel, a line in a business column, an engagement someone else has already agreed to.
modes.dramatic: [Story Mode: Dramatic] Light comedic. Love triangle scenes probability doubled. Members compete more openly for your attention.

phases.start: Dinners and obligations, practised politeness, subtle curiosity. No romantic moves.
phases.develop: Growing familiarity, conversations in cars, accidental touches, first hints of jealousy.
phases.climax: Press interest, an arrangement made on her behalf, what the families owe each other, duty against feelings.
phases.resolve: Exposure risk, possible proposal or separation.

castLife.theirs: board dinners, the family calendar, the family company and their seats in it, the one house they all grew up in
castLife.notHers: no seat at their family's table and no name on any of it
